'''Snehasikta Swarnakar''' (born 1963) is an Indian chemical biologist and the senior principal scientist at the Division of Cancer Biology and Inflammatory Disorder of the [[Indian Institute of Chemical Biology]]. Known for her studies in the field of gastric, ovarian, head and neck cancers, Swarnakar is an elected fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and the West Bengal Academy of Science and Technology. The [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India awarded her the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for her contributions to biosciences in 2007.

== Biography ==
[[File:Aurobindo Bhavan - Main Administrative Building - Jadavpur University - Kolkata 2015-01-08 2401.JPG|thumb|left|Aurobindo Bhavan - Main Administrative Building - [[Jadavpur University]].]]
Snehasikta Swarnakar, born in 1963<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |title=NASI fellows |date=2017-12-21 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-12-21 |archive-date=16 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160316043224/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=S |url-status=dead }}</ref> in the Indian state of [[West Bengal]], secured a PhD in 1993 from [[Jadavpur University]] for her thesis, ''Studies on a sialic acid-binding lectin from albumin gland of apple snail Pila globosa'',<ref name="Editorial Board - JPBMS">{{Cite web |url=http://www.jpbms.info/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=62&Itemid=49 |title=Editorial Board - JPBMS |last=Administrator |date=2017-12-24 |website=www.jpbms.info |language=en-gb |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> working on junior and senior research fellowships from the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]]<ref name="Link - IICB">{{Cite web |url=https://www.noexperiencenecessarybook.com/VGVBr/link-iicb.html |title=Link - IICB |date=2017-12-24 |website=www.noexperiencenecessarybook.com |language=en-US |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> and moved to the US for her post-doctoral work which she completed at the [[University of California, Davis]] and [[Marine Biological Laboratory]] during 1994–97.<ref name="Snehasikta Swarnakar - Senior Principal Scientist">{{Cite web |url=http://iicb.res.in/index.php/2017/04/20/snehasikta-swarnakar/ |title=Snehasikta Swarnakar - Senior Principal Scientist |date=2017-12-24 |website=iicb.res.in |language=en-US |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> She started her career in 1997 as a research scientist at the [[Stony Brook University]] where she worked until 2001 and on her return to India, she joined the Division of Cancer Biology and Inflammatory Disorder of the [[Indian Institute of Chemical Biology]] where she holds the position of a senior principal scientist. In between, she had two stints as a visiting scientist abroad; first at the [[Scripps Research Institute]] in 2002 and then at the [[University of Connecticut]] in 2007. She is also a visiting professor at the Department of Environmental Science of the [[University of Calcutta]].<ref name="Environmental Science - Guest faculty">{{Cite web |url=http://www.caluniv.ac.in/academic/department/Environmental-Sc.html |title=Environmental Science - Guest faculty |date=2017-12-24 |website=www.caluniv.ac.in |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref>

Swarnakar resides along Lake Road in Kolkata.<ref name="NASI fellows" />

== Legacy ==
[[File:Curcuma longa roots.jpg|thumb|235px|Turmeric rhizome and powder]]
Swarnakar's research is focused on cancer biology and she is known to have conducted basic and translational research on various types of cancers such as [[Lung cancer|lung]], [[Brain cancer|brain]], [[Oral cancer|oral]], [[Breast cancer|breast]], [[Pancreatic cancer|pancreatic]], [[Blood cancer|blood]] and [[cervical cancer]]s.<ref name="Cancer Biology & Inflammatory Disorder">{{Cite web |url=http://iicb.res.in/index.php/cancer-biology-and-inflammatory-disorder-2/ |title=Cancer Biology & Inflammatory Disorder |date=2017-12-24 |website=iicb.res.in |language=en-US |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> 
She led a team of scientists who worked on the therapeutic properties of [[turmeric]] and they identified that the controlled dosage of [[curcumin]], an ingredient of turmeric which gave the [[rhizome]] its yellow color, acted as a therapeutic agent for [[gastric]] [[inflammation]] and [[Gastric ulcer|ulceration]].<ref name="Turmeric Can Soothe Gastric Inflammation, Ulcers">{{Cite news |url=https://www.indiatimes.com/health/buzz/turmeric-can-soothe-gastric-inflammation-ulcers-239284.html |title=Turmeric Can Soothe Gastric Inflammation, Ulcers |date=26 September 2012 |work=indiatimes.com |access-date=2017-12-24 |language=en}}</ref> They demonstrated that curcumin increased [[MMP2]] enzyme level while deceasing the [[MMP9]] enzyme, thus ensured balance of the two enzymes which acted in opposite ways in the formation of new blood vessels. They also proposed a treatment protocol for [[gastric ulcers]] with the use of  [[nanocapsules]] and [[antioxidants]] where [[quercetin]], an antioxidant present in apples, tomatoes and onions is administered through nanocapsules to treat ethanol-induced gastric ulcers.<ref name="Nanocapsules the next big thing to prevent alcohol-related gastric ulcers">{{Cite news |url=http://www.indiamedicaltimes.com/2012/10/09/nanocapsules-the-next-big-thing-to-prevent-alcohol-related-gastric-ulcers/ |title=Nanocapsules the next big thing to prevent alcohol-related gastric ulcers |date=9 October 2012 |work=India Medical Times |access-date=2017-12-24 |language=en-US}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|The antioxidant cleaned the [[reactive oxygen species]] (ROS), a chemically reactive [[Chemical species|species]] that contained oxygen}} Her studies have been documented by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of scientific articles has listed 103 of them.<ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Snehasikta_Swarnakar |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017-12-21 |access-date=2017-12-21}}</ref> Besides, she has contributed chapters to books edited by others.<ref name="DhallaChakraborti2013">{{cite book|author1=Naranjan S. Dhalla|author2=Sajal Chakraborti (Eds)|author3=Sibani Sarkar, Somnath Chatterjee, Snehasikta Swarnakar (chapter authors)|title=Role of Proteases in Cellular Dysfunction|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UeG5BAAAQBAJ&pg=PA67|date=22 November 2013|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|language=en|isbn=978-1-4614-9099-9|pages=67–|chapter=Matrix Metalloproteinases in Ischemia - Reperfusion Injury in Brain: Anti-oxidants as Rescuer}}</ref><ref name="Gupta2012">{{Cite book |title=Matrix Metalloproteinase Inhibitors: Specificity of Binding and Structure-Activity Relationships |last1=Satya Prakash Gupta (Ed.) |last2=Snehasikta Swarnakar, Amartya Mishra, Susri Ray Chaudhuri (Eds) |series=Experientia Supplementum |date=7 April 2012 |volume=103 |pages=57–82 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-0348-0363-2 |language=en |chapter=The Gelatinases and Their Inhibitors: The Structure–Activity Relationships|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-0364-9_3 }}</ref> She has also delivered invited or plenary speeches at science conferences<ref name="14th Annual Meeting of SFRR-India">{{Cite web |url=http://www.sfrr.org/downloads/SFRR_India_2016_Meeting_Report_Information.pdf |title=14th Annual Meeting of SFRR-India |date=January 2016 |website=SFRR-India}}</ref><ref name="4th APSAAR-/ 5th IDARS Conference">{{Cite web |title=4th APSAAR - 5th IDARS Conference |date=2015 |website=APSAAR }}</ref> and has mentored several scholars in their post-graduate and doctoral studies.<ref name="List of AcSIR Students">{{Cite web |url=http://acsir.res.in/student-list/ |title=List of AcSIR Students |date=2017-12-24 |website=AcSIR |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref>

Swarnakar is member of the governing body of the ANB Memorial Foundation, a trust in memory of [[Amar Nath Bhaduri]], the noted chemical biologist<ref name="AN Bhaduri Memorial Foundation">{{Cite web |url=http://anbhaduri.org/index.php?action=foundation&o=4&s=2 |title=AN Bhaduri Memorial Foundation |date=2017-12-24 |website=anbhaduri.org |language=en |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> she was the secretary of the organizing committee of the 2nd International Meet on Advanced Studies on Cell Signaling Network (CeSiN 2014) held in Kolkata.<ref name="International Conference Cesin 2014">{{Cite web |url=http://snehasiktaswarnakar.wixsite.com/cesin2014/committee |title=International Conference Cesin 2014 |date=2017-12-24 |website=International Conference Cesin 2014 |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> She is the treasurer of the West Bengal Academy of Science and Technology<ref name="WAST Executive Council">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iicb.res.in/wast/present_council.html |title=WAST Executive Council |date=2017-12-24 |website=www.iicb.res.in |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> and sits in the council of the Chemical Biology Society.<ref name="Chemical Biology Society">{{Cite web |url=http://www.cbs-india.org/members.html |title=Chemical Biology Society |date=2017-12-24 |website=www.cbs-india.org |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> She is also a life member of the [[Indian Science Congress Association]], the Biotech Research Society, India, the Society for Free Radical Research, the [[International Society for Computational Biology]] and the Society of Biological Chemists, India.<ref name="Link - IICB" />

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Department of Biotechnology]] of the Government of India awarded her the [[National Bioscience Award for Career Development]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 2007.<ref name="Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development">{{Cite web |url=http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |title=Awardees of National Bioscience Awards for Career Development |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Biotechnology |access-date=2017-11-20 |archive-date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191331/http://dbtindia.nic.in/wp-content/uploads/2014/03/list_of_bioscience_awardees.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> She was elected as a fellow by the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] in 2012<ref name="NASI Year Book 2015">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI Year Book 2015 |date=2017-12-17 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=2017-12-17 |archive-date=6 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150806211716/http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> and was one of the team members of [[Anirban Bandyopadhyay]] who won the Palo Alto Longevity Prize in 2013.<ref name="Palo Alto Longevity Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://paloaltoprize.com/team/ajochhand |title=Palo Alto Longevity Prize |date=2017-12-24 |website=paloaltoprize.com |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref> She is also an elected fellow of the West Bengal Academy of Science and Technology.<ref name="WAST fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.iicb.res.in/wast/fellow_wast.pdf |title=WAST fellows |date=2017-12-24 |website=West Bengal Academy of Science and Technology |access-date=2017-12-24}}</ref>
